newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil power/telecom selloffs seen raising $79 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil power/telecom selloffs seen raising $79 bln.

text.p: Privatization of Brazil's power and telecommunications industries should raise nearly $80 billion over the next three years, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said Wednesday.

In the last year and a half, the combined value of receipts raised by the sale of state-owned companies and of their debts rose to $15.3 billion, up from $13.5 billion in the previous five years, Kandir told a news conference.
"The expectation is that we will speed up privatization even more and the privatization of power and telecommunications in the next three years will raise $79 billion," he said.
Kandir said the sale of the Telebras system, excluding long-distance carrier Embratel, would raise about $17 billion.
Embratel was worth about $6.0 billion and fees for concessions to run B Band cellular operations would generate another $6.0 billion, he said.
Brazil signed its first B Band concession contract Wednesday. Privatization of the Telebras system is expected to take place in 1998.

Kandir also put a value on the generating assets of the federally owned Eletrobras system, currently being prepared for privatization. Furnas and Eletrosul, both of which are expected to be sold in the first half of 1998, would raise $5.8 billion and $2.3 billion respectively.
Chesf and Eletronorte, slated for privatization in 1999, would produce $7.5 billon and $6.2 billion in receipts, the minister said.
As well as the federal power companies, several states were preparing their power distributors for privatization and they would probably raise about $28.7 billion, he said.
